category.title: Modular Arithmetic & Fast Exponentiation
category.description: Modular properties, negative modulo handling, Fast Binary Exponentiation, Modular Inverse via Fermat's Theorem & Extended GCD, and Chinese Remainder Theorem.

algorithms.title: Modular Arithmetic Operations (Add, Sub, Mul, Div)
algorithms.summary: Safe fundamental modular operations preventing integer overflow and handling negative remainders.
explanation: 1. Modular Addition: `(A + B) % M = ((A % M) + (B % M)) % M`.
2. Modular Subtraction: `(A - B) % M = ((A % M) - (B % M) + M) % M` (adds M to prevent negative result).
3. Modular Multiplication: `(A * B) % M = ((A % M) * (B % M)) % M`.
4. Modular Division: `(A / B) % M = (A * B^(-1)) % M` where `B^(-1)` is the modular inverse of B modulo M.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Prevents integer overflow and negative modulo bugs in competitive programming.
wAnswers.whenToUse: In all problems asking for answer modulo 10^9+7 or 998244353.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Combinatorics, graph counting, dynamic programming DP modulo results.

algorithms.title: Binary Exponentiation (Fast Power (A^B) % M)
algorithms.summary: Computes (A^B) % M in O(log B) logarithmic time by squaring base A and testing binary bits of exponent B.
explanation: 1. Divide & Conquer Bitwise Idea: `A^B = (A^(B/2))^2` if B is even, and `A * A^(B-1)` if B is odd.
2. Binary Bits: Iterate bits of B. If current bit is 1, multiply `res = (res * base) % M`.
3. Square Base: At every step, square `base = (base * base) % M` and halve `B >>= 1`.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Computes huge powers (e.g. A^10^18) in microseconds.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When evaluating powers under modulo or calculating matrix exponentiation.
wAnswers.whereUsed: RSA cryptography, fast Fibonacci matrix exponentiation, combinatorics.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(log B) reduces 10^18 multiplication loops down to just ~60 steps.

algorithms.title: Modular Multiplicative Inverse (Fermat & Ext-GCD)
algorithms.summary: Find integer X such that (A * X) % M = 1 using Fermat's Little Theorem or Extended Euclidean Algorithm.
explanation: 1. Fermat's Little Theorem: If M is prime, `A^(M-1) ≡ 1 (mod M)`. Multiplying by `A^(-1)` yields `A^(-1) ≡ A^(M-2) (mod M)`.
2. Extended GCD Method: Works for any M co-prime to A (`gcd(A, M) = 1`). Solves `A*X + M*Y = 1`.
3. Division Modulo M: Computing `(A / B) % M` is performed as `(A * modInverse(B, M)) % M`.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Enables division modulo M in O(log M) time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When calculating combinations `nCr % M` or dividing under modulo.

algorithms.title: Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT)
algorithms.summary: Solves system of simultaneous congruences X ≡ a_i (mod m_i) for pairwise coprime moduli.
explanation: 1. Problem: Find X such that `X ≡ a1 (mod m1)`, `X ≡ a2 (mod m2)`, ..., `X ≡ ak (mod mk)`.
3. For each equation `i`: Let `M_i = M / m_i`. Compute `y_i = modInverse(M_i, m_i)`.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Solves system of remainder equations across coprime moduli in O(K log M) time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When evaluating large numbers represented by their remainders.
wAnswers.whereUsed: RSA decryption acceleration, multi-precision arithmetic, secret sharing schemes.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Reconstructs unique solution modulo M without brute forcing.
